external_entities.name: member
external_entities.description: A grocery loyalty programme member who uses the mobile app, signs in, approves consent, and spends points on gift cards.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Members collect points when they shop and spend them on gift cards.

external_entities.name: members' phone
external_entities.description: A member's phone running the mobile app and holding its refresh token.
external_entities.source_excerpt: The app keeps a refresh token on the phone.

external_entities.name: partner app
external_entities.description: A web application operated by another company, such as a meal-planning service that shows a member's points.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Partner apps are web applications that other companies run on their own servers

external_entities.name: browser
external_entities.description: The browser used by a member to sign in and approve consent for a partner app.
external_entities.source_excerpt: A member who connects a partner app signs in on the authorization server's sign-in page in their browser

processes.name: mobile app
processes.description: The mobile application that signs members in through the authorization server and calls the rewards API.
processes.source_excerpt: Members use our mobile app. The app signs a member in through our authorization server
processes.notes: Nobody wrote down whether the app sends a PKCE challenge.

processes.name: authorization server
processes.description: The server that signs members in, handles authorization code and consent flows, and issues access and refresh tokens.
processes.source_excerpt: The app signs a member in through our authorization server with the authorization code flow

processes.name: rewards API
processes.description: The API that reads and writes the points ledger and receives requests from the mobile app and partner applications.
processes.source_excerpt: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger

processes.name: support console
processes.description: A web application that closes a member's account.
processes.source_excerpt: The support console is a web app that closes a member's account.

data_stores.name: identity database
data_stores.description: The database containing member accounts, email addresses, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens, consents, and account closure state.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The authorization server keeps member accounts, email addresses and password hashes in the identity database

data_stores.name: points ledger
data_stores.description: The ledger containing every member's balance and every points transaction, including the client associated with each change.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the points ledger, which holds every member's balance and every points transaction

data_stores.name: API log store
data_stores.description: The store containing every request received by the rewards API, including headers.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The rewards API also writes every request it receives, headers included, to the API log store.

data_flows.name: use mobile app
data_flows.description: A member uses the mobile application.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Members use our mobile app.

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.description: The mobile app signs a member in through the authorization server using the authorization code flow.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The app signs a member in through our authorization server with the authorization code flow
data_flows.notes: Nobody wrote down whether the app sends a PKCE challenge.

data_flows.name: call API
data_flows.description: The mobile app calls the rewards API using the access token it received.
data_flows.source_excerpt: then calls the rewards API with the access token it gets back
data_flows.data_description: access token and rewards API requests

data_flows.name: use browser
data_flows.description: A member uses a browser to sign in and approve a partner-app consent request.
data_flows.source_excerpt: A member who connects a partner app signs in on the authorization server's sign-in page in their browser

data_flows.name: approve consent
data_flows.description: The browser accesses the authorization server sign-in page and consent screen for a partner app.
data_flows.source_excerpt: signs in on the authorization server's sign-in page in their browser and approves a consent screen

data_flows.name: return code
data_flows.description: The authorization server returns an authorization code to the partner app's redirect URI.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The browser then returns to the partner app's redirect URI with an authorization code.

data_flows.name: request token
data_flows.description: A partner app sends a token request containing its client secret to the authorization server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The partner app sends that secret in the body of its token requests.

data_flows.name: show points
data_flows.description: A partner app uses the partner API to show a member's points.
data_flows.source_excerpt: such as a meal-planning service that shows a member's points

data_flows.name: issue token
data_flows.description: The authorization server issues an access token to the mobile app.
data_flows.source_excerpt: the access token it gets back

data_flows.name: store identity data
data_flows.description: The authorization server stores member identity data, authorization codes, refresh tokens, consents, and account state.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The authorization server keeps member accounts, email addresses and password hashes in the identity database
data_flows.data_description: accounts, email addresses, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens, consents, and account state

data_flows.name: read-write ledger
data_flows.description: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger, including balances and transactions.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger
data_flows.notes: Nobody recorded how the rewards API connects to the ledger.

data_flows.name: write requests
data_flows.description: The rewards API writes every received request, including headers, to the API log store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The rewards API also writes every request it receives, headers included, to the API log store.

data_flows.name: take token
data_flows.description: The support console obtains access tokens from the authorization server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It takes access tokens from the same authorization server

data_flows.name: close account
data_flows.description: The support console marks a member's account closed in the identity database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Closing an account marks it closed in the identity database.
data_flows.notes: Nobody recorded how the support console connects to the identity database.

trust_boundaries.name: our cloud account
trust_boundaries.description: The organisation's own cloud account where the platform components and stores run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Everything below runs in our own cloud account

trust_boundaries.name: members' phones
trust_boundaries.description: The members' phones, which are outside the organisation's cloud account and hold the mobile app's refresh tokens.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: apart from the members' phones and the partner apps

trust_boundaries.name: partner apps' own servers
trust_boundaries.description: Servers operated by other companies for their partner applications.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: partner apps that other companies run on their own servers

assumptions.assumption: The identity database is confidential because it contains member accounts, email addresses, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens, and consents.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the identity database contains personal information and authentication credentials.

assumptions.assumption: The points ledger is confidential because it contains member balances and points transactions.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the ledger contains every member's balance and every points transaction.

assumptions.assumption: The API log store is confidential because it contains every request and its headers, which may include credentials and personal information.
assumptions.basis: The source states that every request received by the rewards API, headers included, is written to the API log store.

assumptions.assumption: The rewards API is internet-facing because it is served on the same public hostname as the support console.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the support console is served on the same public hostname as the rewards API.

assumptions.assumption: The support console is internet-facing because it is served on a public hostname.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the support console is served on the same public hostname as the rewards API.
